body.en: Robert Frost was an American poet, famous for poems about rural New England life, and a four-time winner of the Pulitzer Prize. In A *Roadside Stand*, poor country people have set up a little shed by the road, in front of an old house, to sell farm produce to city people passing in cars. Through it they hope to earn some city money.

points.en: Setting: a country road used by city traffic
A small shed selling farm produce

say.en: In the centre: the roadside stand.
They sell wild berries in small wooden boxes.
They sell golden squash, crook-necked and warty.
A crude, home-made sign has letters painted the wrong way.
The sellers are poor rural people.
They hope city money will improve their lives.
They dream of the better life they see in films.

body.en: The stand is not mainly a cry for charity; the *sellers* want a fair chance to earn. They long for the kind of comfortable life they imagine city people live, a life they see in the cinema. Their hope makes their neglect by the passers-by all the more painful.

problem.en: Why did the rural people put up the roadside stand?

steps.en: State the purpose: to sell farm produce to passing city people.
Explain the deeper wish: to earn city money.
Add the dream: a better life like the one they see in films.

answer.en: They put up the stand to sell wild berries, squash and other produce to city people driving past. They hoped to earn some city money and so improve their lives, moving closer to the comfortable life they had seen in films.
